crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Personalised Wealth Advice
children.blurb: Personalised wealth advice in portfolio construction tailors asset allocation, risk exposure, and rebalancing to an individual client's goals, constraints, tax situation, and time horizon.

children.name: Portfolio Optimisation Beyond Mean and Variance
children.blurb: Portfolio optimisation beyond mean and variance moves away from Markowitz's two-moment model to account for skewness, kurtosis, tail risk, and non-normal return distributions.

children.name: Tail Risk Hedging
children.blurb: Tail risk hedging in AI portfolio construction is the practice of reducing exposure to rare but severe losses that can hit concentrated AI equity, credit, or venture positions.

children.name: Sustainability Factors in Portfolios
children.blurb: Sustainability factors in portfolios refer to environmental, social and governance criteria used alongside financial metrics when selecting and weighting assets, including AI-related instruments.

children.name: Pricing Illiquid Assets
children.blurb: Pricing illiquid assets covers positions that do not trade on an active exchange, such as private AI company equity, venture fund interests, restricted stock, intellectual property, data rights, and thinly traded tokens.

sections.body: Portfolio construction in AI economics is the practical use of machine learning to assemble and adjust holdings. Personalised Wealth Advice uses models to match portfolios to an individual's stated goals and constraints, not to guarantee returns. Portfolio Optimisation Beyond Mean and Variance replaces simple expected return and volatility with measures that capture skew, tail dependence and illiquidity. Tail Risk Hedging uses AI to identify and price instruments that may offset large losses. Sustainability Factors in Portfolios applies classifiers and natural language processing to company disclosures and news. Pricing Illiquid Assets uses models to estimate values for assets that rarely trade, such as private credit or real assets.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Personalised advice is operational in many robo-advisory systems, but it mostly rebalances among standard funds rather than solving for true individual utility. Optimisation beyond mean and variance is well studied in academic code, yet production systems still rely heavily on covariance matrices that break in stress. Tail risk hedging remains unsolved in the sense that no model reliably predicts rare crashes, and hedges often cost more than they protect. Sustainability factors are measurable but contested, because different data vendors score the same company differently. Pricing illiquid assets has improved with more data, but honest limits remain where there is no transaction history. The site tracks 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices, which is a narrow slice of the assets these methods would need to handle.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking for how AI tailors portfolios to a person would start with Personalised Wealth Advice, which explains the inputs and outputs of advisory models. Portfolio Optimisation Beyond Mean and Variance then shows why the standard risk model is not enough and what alternatives are being tested. Tail Risk Hedging connects to that page by focusing on the extreme losses that mean-variance ignores. Sustainability Factors in Portfolios covers a different axis, where non-financial preferences and disclosures enter the construction process. Pricing Illiquid Assets sits at the edge, because many of the assets in the other pages, especially private and alternative holdings, need a value before any optimisation or hedging can run. Together the pages move from the individual client to the mathematical core, then to risk extremes, then to values and finally to the assets that are hardest to price.
